01-001.r: Regulating Act 1773 → Supreme Court at Fort William, Calcutta; set up in 1774; first Chief Justice Sir Elijah Impey.

01-003.r: Regulating Act 1773 → Supreme Court; Pitt's India Act 1784 → Board of Control; Charter Act 1813 → English missionaries allowed; Charter Act 1833 → Law Member in GG's Council.
01-003.h: Court → Control → Christians → Codes: the four Acts in time order.

01-004.r: English education came from all three: Charter Act 1813 (Rs 1 lakh a year for education), General Committee of Public Instruction 1823, and the Orientalist-Anglicist Controversy.

01-005.r: Charter Act 1813 → ended East India Company's trade monopoly in India, except tea and China trade; Charter Act 1833 ended its commercial role altogether.
01-005.t: Don't confuse 1813 (monopoly ended except tea and China) with 1833 (Company left with political functions only).

01-006.r: Charter Act 1813 → Company lost its trade monopoly with India but kept monopoly of trade with China and in tea.

01-007.r: Charter Act 1813: ended trade monopoly (except tea, China) and asserted British Crown sovereignty over Company territories; territory and revenue stayed with Company for 20 more years.

01-008.r: Charter Act 1833, Section 87 → no Indian barred from Company posts for religion, birth, descent or colour; first opening for Indians in administration.

02-001.r: Indian Councils Act 1861 → portfolio system (five members, sixth added 1874); 6 to 12 additional members for legislation; no split of State and Central subjects.
02-001.t: Statement that the Executive Council became 7 members is false.

02-002.r: Indian Councils Act 1892: royal assent 20 June 1892, in force 3 February 1893 (so statement i is wrong); additional members ten to sixteen, at least half non-official.
02-002.c: Answer not printed; explanation only rules out statement (i), which leaves option (d) Only (ii).

02-003.r: Indian Councils Act 1892 → Legislative Council could discuss the Budget but not vote on it; questions with 6 days' notice; no supplementary questions.

02-004.r: Indian Councils Act 1909 (Minto-Morley Reforms) → separate electorate for Muslims (communal representation); sowed seeds of separatism and partition.

02-006.r: Federal Court → created by Government of India Act 1935; started 1st October 1937; first Chief Justice Sir Maurice Gwyer.
02-006.t: Options list only 1861, 1909, 1919 Acts, so the answer is 'None of the above'.

02-008.r: Dyarchy at the Centre → Government of India Act 1935 (never implemented); it abolished the provincial dyarchy of the 1919 Act.
02-008.t: Don't confuse: 1919 Act = dyarchy in provinces; 1935 Act = dyarchy at Centre.

02-010.r: Government of India Act 1919 (Montagu-Chelmsford) → dyarchy in provincial executive and devolution of legislative authority to provinces; separate Muslim electorates were not its feature.

02-011.r: Dyarchy (Greek 'di-arche' = double rule) → provincial subjects split into 'reserved' (Governor and executive council) and 'transferred' categories.

02-012.r: 1919 Act reserved subjects: administration of justice, land revenue, police, press; transferred: local self-government, public works, health and sanitation, education.

02-013.r: Dyarchy in provinces → Government of India Act 1919 (Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms); reserved subjects included law and order, finance, land revenue, irrigation.

02-014.r: Government of India Act 1919 → central legislature bicameral for the first time: Council of State (upper, 60 members) and Legislative Assembly (lower).

02-016.r: Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms 1919 gave women no voting rights; Government of India Act 1935 gave women reserved seats in legislature.

02-017.r: Government of India Act 1919 → separate ICS exam held in India; by 1941 Indians outnumbered Europeans in ICS; merit-based exams began in London in 1855.

02-018.r: Chamber of Princes (120 members) → Act of 1919; set up by George V's Proclamation, 23 December 1919; forum for rulers of princely states.

02-019.r: Central Legislative Assembly elections under Government of India Act 1919 → 1926 and 1945 (not 1937).

02-020.r: Last election of the central Indian legislature under Government of India Act 1919 → 1945.

02-021.r: President's ordinance power (Art. 123) → relic of Section 42, Government of India Act 1935; the Viceroy could already issue ordinances under the 1861 Act.

02-022.r: 'Principle of Constitutional Autocracy' → Government of India Act 1935; executive power vested in Governors (provinces) and Governor-General (Centre) for the Crown.

02-023.r: Centre-State distribution of powers in our Constitution → based on Government of India Act 1935, which split legislative powers between central and provincial legislatures.

02-024.r: Government of India Act 1935: residuary powers went to the Viceroy (Governor-General), not to provincial legislatures; it did give All India Federation, provincial autonomy, dyarchy at Centre.

02-025.r: Government of India Act 1935 → provincial autonomy, All India Federation (federal polity) and dyarchy at the Centre; the 1919 Act had only begun provincial autonomy.

02-030.r: Government of India Act 1935 → 'Federation of India' of British Indian Provinces and Princely States (true); defence and foreign affairs were not under the federal legislature (false).

02-032.r: Government of India Act 1935 features: reconstructed Governor General's Executive Council, provincial autonomy, proposed Federation of India; 'Appraisal of the Act of 1935' is not a feature.

02-033.r: Government of India Act 1935 gave no written Constitution; Britain accepted that Indians would frame their own constitution in the August Offer, 1940.

02-034.r: Government of India Act 1935 → main source of the Constitution: federal government, Centre-State division of powers, Federal Court, dyarchy at Centre.

02-035.r: Government of India Act 1935 → bicameral legislatures in 6 provinces: Bihar, Bengal, United Provinces, Bombay, Madras, Assam.
02-035.c: Answer not printed; explanation favours (c) 1935 Act but notes the Bihar Legislative Council website credits the 1919 Act.

02-036.r: Burma separated from India in 1937 under the Government of India Act 1935.

03-001.r: First Indian demand for a Constituent Assembly → Swaraj Party, Ranchi conference, May 1934; members to be elected on adult suffrage.

03-002.r: Idea of a Constituent Assembly first given by M.N. Roy in 1934; first formal demand by Swaraj Party, Ranchi, May 1934.
03-002.t: Don't confuse the person who gave the idea (M.N. Roy) with the party that formally demanded it (Swaraj Party).

03-003.r: Gandhi, 'The Only Way', Harijan, 19 November 1939: only a Constituent Assembly can produce an indigenous Constitution truly representing the people's will.

03-004.r: Proposal to frame India's Constitution by an elected Constituent Assembly (after Second World War) → Cripps Mission, 1942.

03-005.r: Cripps Mission (March 1942): provincial members elected (not nominated) by provincial assemblies, princes nominate; a province rejecting the Constitution could sign separate agreement with Britain.

03-006.r: Cabinet Mission 1946 → Constituent Assembly seats by population: roughly one representative per 10 lakh people.

03-007.r: Cabinet Mission: Pethick-Lawrence (Secretary for India), Stafford Cripps (Board of Trade), A.V. Alexander (Navy); William Wood was not a member.

03-008.r: Constituent Assembly was set up under the Cabinet Mission Plan, 1946, by indirect election.

03-010.r: Interim Government 1946: Viceroy was ex-officio President of Executive Council; Jawaharlal Nehru was Vice-President; announced 24 August, in charge by 2 September 1946.

03-011.r: Interim Government (announced 24 August 1946): Rajagopalachari – Education, Rajendra Prasad – Food and Agriculture, Jagjivan Ram – Labour; S. Radhakrishnan not a member.

03-014.r: Wavell Plan (June 1945) → equal Hindu and Muslim members in the Executive Council (true); the claim that Wavell saw this as avoiding partition is false.

03-015.r: Constituent Assembly: indirectly elected by provincial legislative assemblies (not adult suffrage, not direct); multi-party body; worked through many committees.

03-016.r: Constituent Assembly: not based on adult franchise; indirectly elected; multi-party (Congress, Muslim League, independents); worked through several committees.

03-017.r: Constituent Assembly was not elected on universal adult franchise; provincial legislators who elected it had limited franchise (education, property, tax) under the 1935 Act.

03-018.r: Constituent Assembly members → elected by provincial legislative assemblies, roughly one seat per million people; 292 from provinces, 4 from Chief Commissioners' provinces.

03-021.r: Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha (oldest member) → Provisional President at the first meeting, 9 December 1946, Constitution Hall, New Delhi; then Rajendra Prasad took over.

03-022.r: First meeting (9 December 1946) chaired by Dr. Sachchidanand Sinha (temporary); Dr. Rajendra Prasad elected permanent Chairman 11 December 1946, proposed by J.B. Kripalani.
03-022.t: Don't confuse temporary chairman (Sinha) with first elected chairman (Prasad).

03-027.r: First meeting → 9 December 1946, Constitution Hall (now Central Hall), New Delhi; Nehru was a member from day one and moved Objective Resolution 13 December 1946; President: Rajendra Prasad.

03-030.r: Frank Anthony → first nominated (temporary) Deputy Chairman, 9 December 1946, nominated by Sachchidanand Sinha; H.C. Mukherjee → first permanent Vice-President.

03-031.r: Constituent Assembly first met (was established) 9 December 1946; first session ran to 23 December 1946 with 207 members; Nehru moved Objective Resolution in fifth meeting.

03-036.r: Objective Resolution → moved by Nehru on 13 December 1946 in the fifth meeting of the first session; later became the Preamble.

03-037.r: Objectives Resolution: moved by Nehru 13 December 1946; adopted unanimously 22 January 1947; its amended form is the Preamble.
03-037.h: Moved in December 1946, passed in January 1947: about six weeks apart.

03-038.r: Resolution for India's Constitution (Objectives Resolution) → adopted unanimously 22 January 1947; presented by Nehru 13 December 1946.
03-038.t: Don't pick 22 January 1946: the Assembly first met only in December 1946.

03-039.r: Preamble's basis before the Drafting Committee → Nehru's Objectives Resolution (13 December 1946; passed 22 January 1947).

03-041.r: Nehru's Objectives Resolution shaped the Constitution; Preamble states its aims; people of India gave it. False: head of State (President) is elected indirectly, not by people.

03-042.r: 11 sessions (165 days) up to adoption, 26 November 1949, plus a final sitting 24 January 1950 for signatures → 12 sessions; time taken 2 years 11 months 18 days.
03-042.c: Explanation gives 2 years 11 months 17 days, while the also-asked answers give 18 days.

03-046.r: Final session of Constituent Assembly → 24 January 1950: Constitution signed and Dr. Rajendra Prasad declared elected President of India.

03-047.r: H.C. Mukherjee → first Vice-President of Constituent Assembly; K.M. Munshi → only Congress member of Drafting Committee; V.T. Krishnamachari → Rajasthan princely states; Nehru → Union Constitution Committee.
03-047.t: Frank Anthony was the temporary (nominated) Vice-President; H.C. Mukherjee the regular one.

03-048.r: Constitutional Advisor of the Constituent Assembly → Sir Benegal Narsing Rau (B.N. Rau).

03-049.r: First draft of the Constitution → B.N. Rau (constitutional advisor): 243 Articles and 13 Schedules, placed before the Drafting Committee.

03-050.r: Third reading of the Constitution → began 17 November 1949, completed 26 November 1949.
03-050.c: Answer not printed; none of the four options is correct (no option has 17 November 1949).

03-051.r: Constitution adopted, enacted and completed → 26 November 1949 (date in Preamble); citizenship, interim Parliament and transitional provisions came into force that day.

03-056.r: Constitution came into force fully on 26 January 1950; adopted by the Constituent Assembly on 26 November 1949.
03-056.t: Don't confuse adoption (26 November 1949) with commencement (26 January 1950).

03-057.r: 26 January chosen for commencement → Congress had observed it as Independence Day (Purna Swaraj) in 1930, after the Lahore Session, December 1929.

03-058.r: Constitution Day → 26 November, the day the Constituent Assembly adopted the Constitution in 1949.

03-059.r: Constitution Day (Samvidhan Divas) 26 November, notified 19 November 2015 by Social Justice Ministry, marks adoption in 1949; Drafting Committee was not set up that day.

03-060.r: Constitution adopted and enacted by the Constituent Assembly (11th session) on 26 November 1949, as stated in the Preamble itself.

03-063.r: Order: Assembly first met 9 December 1946 → Drafting Committee 29 August 1947 → adopted 26 November 1949 → commenced 26 January 1950.

03-064.r: Ambedkar → first elected from East Bengal (1946); after Partition elected from Pune seat of Bombay Presidency, vacated by M.R. Jaikar.

03-065.r: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar → born 14 April 1891, Mhow (Dr. Ambedkar Nagar), Madhya Pradesh; died 6 December 1956, Delhi.

03-066.r: Third Round Table Conference (November-December 1932, London) → led to Government of India Act 1935, which proposed All India Federation of British Provinces and Princely States.

03-067.r: Constitution meets all the nation's needs (amendable) and is called an 'Adopted Constitution' (borrows from many constitutions); both true, but R does not explain A.

03-068.r: Maulana Azad → urged deferring adult franchise for 15 years in the Constituent Assembly; Rajendra Prasad and Nehru backed its adoption.

03-069.r: Mahatma Gandhi → advised disbanding the Indian National Congress as a political party after Independence.

03-070.r: 'A Constitution, like a machine, is a lifeless thing...' → Dr. Rajendra Prasad, speech at adoption of the Constitution, 26 November 1949.

03-071.r: 'Founding Fathers tended to minimize minority interests' → Sir Ivor Jennings, on minority protections in the Constitution.

03-072.r: 'Constituent Assembly was Congress and Congress was India' → Granville Austin, in his book 'The Indian Constitution'.

03-073.r: Women members in the Constituent Assembly → 15, e.g. Sarojini Naidu, Hansa Mehta, Durgabai Deshmukh, Rajkumari Amrit Kaur, Sucheta Kripalani, Vijayalakshmi Pandit.

04-001.r: Union Constitution Committee → Nehru; Rules of Procedure and Steering Committees → Rajendra Prasad; States Committee → Nehru; Drafting Committee → Ambedkar.

04-002.r: Provincial Constitution Committee → Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel; Drafting Committee → Dr. B.R. Ambedkar.

04-005.r: Union Constitution Committee → Nehru; Rules of Procedure → Rajendra Prasad; Drafting → Ambedkar; Fundamental Rights Sub-committee → J.B. Kripalani.

04-006.r: Advisory Committee on Fundamental Rights, Minorities, Tribal and Excluded Areas → Sardar Patel; Steering → Rajendra Prasad; Union Powers → Nehru; Drafting → Ambedkar.
04-006.c: Answer not printed: Steering Committee chairman (Rajendra Prasad) is not in List-II, so no option is correct.

04-007.r: Advisory Committee on Fundamental Rights, Minorities, Tribals and Excluded Areas → Sardar Patel; sub-committees: Fundamental Rights → J.B. Kripalani, Minorities → H.C. Mukherjee.

04-008.r: Drafting Committee: Ambedkar + 6 members: N. Gopalaswami Ayyangar, Alladi Krishnaswamy Ayyar, K.M. Munshi, Mohd. Saadullah, B.L. Mitter, D.P. Khaitan (later N. Madhava Rao, T.T. Krishnamachari).

04-010.r: K.M. Munshi → member of the Drafting Committee (formed 29 August 1947 under Ambedkar); Jawaharlal Nehru was not a member.

04-012.r: Drafting Committee under Dr. Ambedkar → set up by a resolution on 29 August 1947 to decide the form and structure of the Constitution.

04-013.r: Ad-hoc Committee on National Flag (23 June 1947) → Dr. Rajendra Prasad; earlier Flag Committee (Karachi Session, 2 April 1931) → Sardar Patel.

05-001.r: The Constitution is supreme in India's political system: the supreme law that frames all government institutions, rights, directives and duties.

05-002.r: Judicial Review → borrowed from the USA; courts can declare unconstitutional actions of legislature or executive null and void.

05-003.r: System of judicial review exists in both India and the USA.

05-004.r: Common to India and USA → a federal Supreme Court to interpret the Constitution; USA has dual citizenship and dual judiciary, no three lists; India has single citizenship.

05-005.r: Indian federal system (federalism) → inspired by the Constitution of Canada.

05-007.r: 'Union of States' (Art. 1(1): India, that is Bharat, shall be a Union of States) → from British North America Act, 1867 (Canadian Constitution).

05-008.r: Concurrent List → borrowed from Australia; in Seventh Schedule; originally 47 items, now 52.

05-012.r: Directive Principles of State Policy → borrowed from Ireland; Part IV, Articles 36-51; not enforceable in courts.

05-013.r: DPSP (Part IV, Arts 36-51) → from the Irish Constitution; not justiciable, but the State must apply them in making laws.
05-013.h: Ireland → Instructions to the State: both start with I.

05-016.r: Nomination to Rajya Sabha for talent, experience and service → inspired by the Irish Republic.

05-017.r: Fundamental Rights → USA; Parliamentary system → UK; Emergency provisions → Germany (Weimar); DPSP → Ireland.

05-018.r: Residual powers with the Centre → from Canada, not Australia; Canada also gave strong-centre federation, Governor appointed by Centre, SC advisory jurisdiction.

05-019.r: Fundamental Rights → US Bill of Rights; DPSP → Irish Constitution; Cabinet government → British Constitution; Union-State relations → Canadian Constitution.

05-020.r: Rule of Law → England; Procedure established by law → Japan; Governor reserving bills for President → Canada; Concurrent List → Australia.
05-020.h: Japan gave the procedure: 'J for Just procedure'.

05-021.r: DPSP → Ireland; Fundamental Rights → USA; Concurrent List → Australia; Union of States with stronger Union → Canada.

05-022.r: Fundamental Duties → from the USSR (Russian) Constitution; added by 42nd Amendment, 1976, on Swaran Singh Committee's advice.

05-023.r: Indian Constitution is the world's longest written one (originally 22 Parts, 395 Articles, 8 Schedules); FR chapter borrowed from USA, but that is not why it is long.

05-024.r: Fundamental Rights (Part III, Arts 12-35) → from USA: Equality 14-18, Freedom 19-22, Against Exploitation 23-24, Religion 25-28, Culture and Education 29-30.

05-026.r: Idea of Fundamental Rights (Part III) → taken from the Constitution of the USA.

05-028.r: Election Commission is not borrowed from any foreign constitution; the method of electing the President is inspired by Ireland.

05-029.r: First written Constitution of the world → USA; also the shortest written one, with only 7 Articles.

06-001.r: Original Constitution → 22 Parts, 395 Articles and 8 Schedules.

06-002.r: Order of Parts: I Union and its territory (Arts 1-4) → II Citizenship (5-11) → III Fundamental Rights (12-35) → IV DPSP (36-51) → IV-A Fundamental Duties (51-A).

06-003.r: Fundamental Duties → Part IV-A (inserted 1976), not Part VI-A; Part II Citizenship, Part III Fundamental Rights, Part VI The States.
06-003.t: Don't confuse Part IV-A (Fundamental Duties) with Part VI (The States).

06-004.r: Part IV-A → Fundamental Duties (Art. 51A); Part VI → The States (Arts 152-237); Municipalities → Part IX-A (Arts 243P-243ZG), not Part XI (Union-State relations).

06-005.r: Three-tier Panchayat system → Part IX, by 73rd Amendment 1992 (rural local government); 74th Amendment → urban local bodies (Nagarpalikas).

06-006.r: Part XI → Union-State relations: Chapter I legislative relations, Chapter II administrative relations; Part XII → Finance, Property, Contracts and Suits.

06-007.r: Abolition of Titles → Fundamental Rights; village panchayats → DPSP; education opportunity for child aged 6-14 → Fundamental Duties; 'India, that is Bharat' → Union and its Territory.

06-008.r: Part II → Citizenship; Part III → Fundamental Rights; Part IV → DPSP; Part IV-A → Fundamental Duties; Part V → The Union.

06-009.r: Union Territories → Part VIII, not Part VII; Citizenship → Part II; Municipalities → Part IX-A; Elections → Part XV.

06-010.r: Elections → Part XV (Articles 324-329): Election Commission, electoral rolls, elections to Parliament, State Legislatures, President and Vice-President.

06-011.r: Part IX → Panchayats; Part VIII → Union Territories; Part IV-A → Fundamental Duties; Part IX-A → Municipalities.

06-012.r: Tribunals → Part XIV-A (Arts 323-A, 323-B), added by 42nd Amendment, 1976, not Part XI (Centre-State relations).
06-012.t: Don't confuse Part X (Scheduled and Tribal Areas) with Part XI (Centre-State relations).

06-013.r: Panchayats → Part IX; Municipalities → Part IX-A; Co-operative Societies → Part IX-B; Tribunals → Part XIV-A, not Part X (Scheduled and Tribal Areas).
06-013.h: IX family: IX villages, IX-A towns, IX-B co-operatives.

06-016.r: Fundamental Rights → Part III; Fundamental Duties → Part IV-A; The Union → Part V; Emergency provisions → Part XVIII.

06-017.r: Attorney General → Part V (Art. 76), not Part XIII; Part XIII → Trade, Commerce and Intercourse; Part XIV → Services under Union and States.

06-018.r: Part XV → Elections; Part XVI → Special provisions for certain classes; Part XVII → Official Language; Part XVIII → Emergency provisions.
06-018.h: XV to XVIII in order: Elect → Special classes → Speech (language) → Emergency.

06-019.r: Part XVI (Articles 330-342) → special provisions relating to certain classes.

06-020.r: All true: Municipalities' powers → Part IX-A (Art. 243W; taxes Art. 243X); Emergency provisions → Part XVIII; amendment of Constitution → Part XX.

07-001.r: Original Constitution: 22 Parts, 395 Articles, 8 Schedules; now about 468 Articles (added as 21A, 43B etc.) and 12 Schedules → 'more than 400 Articles'.

07-006.r: Formation of new States → Art. 3; Citizenship → Part II; Fundamental Rights → Part III; Administrative Tribunals → Art. 323-A.

07-007.r: Art. 117 → a Bill imposing tax needs the President's recommendation and cannot be introduced in the Council of States.

07-008.r: Special provisions for Financial Bills → Art. 117; Art. 121 → no discussion in Parliament on judges' conduct; Art. 123 → ordinances.

07-009.r: All India Services → Art. 312; Parliament creates them after a Rajya Sabha resolution backed by two-thirds of members present and voting.

07-010.r: Election Commission → Art. 324 (Part XV, Arts 324-329): Chief Election Commissioner plus other Commissioners fixed by President; Supreme Court → Art. 124.

07-011.r: Separation of Judiciary from Executive → Art. 50, not 48; Art. 48 → agriculture and animal husbandry; Art. 39A legal aid; Art. 40 panchayats; Art. 44 Uniform Civil Code.

07-012.r: Art. 124 → Union Judiciary (Supreme Court); Art. 5 → Citizenship; Art. 352 → Emergency; Art. 245 → distribution of legislative powers.

07-013.r: Art. 14 → Right to Equality; Art. 36 → Directive Principles; Art. 74 → Council of Ministers; Art. 368 → Amendment procedure.

07-014.r: Art. 2 → admit new States by law; Art. 14 → right to equality; Art. 22 → protection against arrest and detention; Art. 111 → President's assent to Bills.

07-015.r: Art. 54 → election of President; Art. 75 → appointment of PM and ministers; Art. 155 → appointment of Governor; Art. 164 → appointment of CM and State ministers.

07-016.r: Art. 61 → impeachment of President; Art. 67(b) → removal of Vice-President; Art. 94 → removal of Speaker; Art. 90 → removal of Deputy Chairman, Rajya Sabha.

07-017.r: Art. 324 → Election Commission; Art. 315 → Public Service Commissions; Art. 280 → Finance Commission; Art. 338 → National Commission for Scheduled Castes.

07-018.r: Art. 323-A → Administrative Tribunals; Art. 324 → Elections; Art. 330 → SC/ST seat reservation in Lok Sabha; Art. 320 → functions of Public Service Commissions.

07-019.r: Consolidated Fund of India → Art. 266; Finance Commission → Art. 280; Financial Emergency → Art. 360; CAG → Art. 148.

07-020.r: Constitutional Amendment → Art. 368; Finance Commission → Art. 280; Financial Emergency → Art. 360; All India Services → Art. 312.

07-021.r: CAG → Art. 148; Finance Commission → Art. 280; Administrative Tribunal → Art. 323-A; UPSC → Art. 315.

07-022.r: All four are correct: Inter-State Council → Art. 263; Finance Commission → Art. 280; Administrative Tribunal → Art. 323A; UPSC → Art. 315.
07-022.c: No answer printed: every pair is correctly matched; UPPSC's key gave (c), which the book rejects.

07-023.r: Art. 26 → freedom to manage religious affairs; Art. 40 → village panchayats; Art. 98 → Secretariat of Parliament; Art. 239 → administration of Union Territories.

07-024.r: Art. 352 → Proclamation of Emergency; Art. 17 → abolition of untouchability; Art. 78 → PM's duty to inform President; Art. 192 → disqualification of State legislators.
